A flap through the skull joining four burr holes on this skull: the keyhole just above the frontozygomatic suture (Yilmaz 2025, Sevgi 2026; the model's zygomatic process of the frontal bone, raised 6 mm); a frontal hole near the superior orbital rim (Yilmaz 2025; here 20 mm above and 10 mm lateral to the supraorbital notch, 20 mm from the keyhole); a temporal hole on the squama near the zygomatic root (Sevgi 2026; here 14 mm above the level of the foramen spinosum); and a posterior hole below the superior temporal line (Yilmaz 2025: near the coronal suture; here 30 mm behind and 18 mm above the pterion, illustrative). The flap is the oval round the four holes (seen face on, they lie on its margin), a smooth curve as a craniotome cuts it, behind the zygomatic bone, leaving no slot under bone it keeps narrower than 3 mm, the corners where the cranial floor is kept rounded over 2.5 mm and its edge smoothed over 1 mm (illustrative).
